overview.headline: How population counts apportion House seats by equal proportions

keyPoints.point: The Constitution requires an actual Enumeration to apportion representatives with first Meeting of Congress
keyPoints.quote: The actual Enumeration shall be made within three Years after the first Meeting of the Congress of the United States

keyPoints.point: The current method for House seats is the Method of Equal Proportions adopted following 1940
keyPoints.quote: The current method used, the Method of Equal Proportions, was adopted by congress in 1941 following the census of 1940.

keyPoints.point: Each of the states is given one seat from the current total before priority ranking assigns remaining seats
keyPoints.quote: Each of the 50 states is given one seat out of the current total of 435.

keyPoints.point: The multiplier uses division by the square root involving seat count for each next seat
keyPoints.quote: 1 divided by the square root of n(n-1)

keyPoints.point: Priority values come from multiplying state population by the calculated multiplier
keyPoints.quote: The priority value is determined by multiplying the population of a state by a "multiplier."
